text:
maria gonzalez: FYI seeing a CPU-side tail-latency regression on the latest kernel-selector roll. started after the dynamic-kernel-mux change. 95p latency up ~30% on small requests.

jon lee: ugh. can you paste the perf/nsys traces? rough guesses: batching spin, GIL, or kvmiss in prefix cache.

maria gonzalez: attaching quick notes from runs. did: nsys for GPU timeline (no major change), perf on CPU during the spike, and a flamegraph.

maria gonzalez: nsys summary (truncated):
```
Process 12345: main -> lots of GPU kernels as usual, GPU idle not increased.
CPU sampling: heavy in runtime::kernel_mux::choose_variant and BatchCoordinator::wait_for_batch
Context-switches spiked during 95p windows.
```

akshay rao: that points at scheduler/batcher interactions. kernel_mux maybe doing extra cost estimation per-request now? the new code checks quantization profile at request time, which could hit Python/KV cache.

maria gonzalez: correct, the mux does a quick heuristic that queries the model profile store. we thought it was cheap but it does a small Python call path to check metadata and optionally hits the KV prefix cache which is locked.

samantha park: do we have a perf record stackcollapse output? want to see if PyEval or C spinlocks dominate.

maria gonzalez: perf record command I used:
```bash
perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30  # during steady load with 95p spike
perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
```
flame top stacks (text excerpt):
```
runtime::BatchCoordinator::wait_for_batch -> runtime::batcher::coordinator_spin_loop -> futex_wait -> __futex_wait
runtime::kernel_mux::choose_variant -> py::object::call -> PyEval_EvalFrameEx 
kv::PrefixCache::lookup -> Mutex::lock -> futex_wake
```

jon lee: so we have a mixture: futex waits (locking) and Python eval frames. that suggests contention around cache+heuristic. any thread migration/affinity changes?

maria gonzalez: yes, we recently changed the dispatcher to allow kernel selection on the io/manager thread instead of pinning to the worker. that probably increases cross-thread lock contention.

akshay rao: hypothesis: kernel_mux querying prefix cache under global lock while batcher threads contend -> long futex waits -> tail latency. also if kernel selection sometimes chooses int8 path which needs quick reordering, that could add serialization.

samantha park: quick experiments: flip kernel_mux to use a cached, lock-free estimated_variant when available (fallback to full check rarely). did that locally and perf flame shows PyEval frames drop by ~70%. Trying on canary now.

benchbot: automated-run: kernel_mux_canary_2182 deployed to canary-1. Smoke tests: throughput -1.2%, p95 latency -6.8%, p99 latency -22.4% (observed).

jon lee: promising. Maria, can you also capture a perf timeline with +- userspace stacks annotated? want to confirm futex hotspots map to specific lines.

maria gonzalez: did that, here's the perf script snippet mapped to source (abbreviated):
```
# perf script sample
kernel_mux.cpp:243 runtime::kernel_mux::choose_variant
  -> kernel_mux.cpp:260 // check profile cache
  -> profile_store.py:84 get_model_profile (via pybind)
  -> prefix_cache.cc:112 PrefixCache::lookup
  -> mutex.h:58 lock() // contended
```

maria gonzalez: flamegraph also shows BatchCoordinator spin waiting up the stack while holding the mutex. so batcher threads can pile up behind the cache lock.

akshay rao: two fixes: 1) move lightweight variant estimate into C++ side (no python call) with atomic-read-only snapshot 2) make prefix cache reader-writer or sharded to reduce contention.

samantha park: for immediate mitigation, we lowered batch_wait_timeout from 5ms to 1ms in canary which reduces head-of-line blocking (fast flush). that dropped p99 but increased CPU usage ~6%.

jon lee: tradeoff accepted for now. we should get a proper fix in the runtime. also add an assertion that kernel_mux path must not call into Python during hot path.

maria gonzalez: agreed. action items:
- akshay: prototype lock-free variant estimator (C++) and a small in-memory snapshot of profiles (due EOD tomorrow).
- samantha: benchmark sharded prefix-cache and new sharding factor (due in 2 days).
- jon: revert dispatcher affinity change on canary if we see regressions revert quickly.
- maria: collect more perf samples (perf + flame + nsys) and post to the perf board.

maria gonzalez: quick note: here's minimal repro steps I used to trigger the spike locally:
```bash
# run the small-load generator
./bench/run_small_latency_load.sh --qps 40 --seq-len 32 --duration 120
# attach perf after 30s
perf record -F 99 -p $(pgrep runtime_binary) -g -- sleep 45
```

jon lee: great, thanks. once akshay has a C++ estimator PR we can run the same perf pipeline and compare flamegraphs. :thumbsup:

maria gonzalez: will post results later today. thanks all.
